title: On the classification of solutions to a class of $N$-Liouville equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
summary: Given $N\geq 2$ and $α>-1$, we consider the following weighted Liouville-type equation involving the $N$-Laplacian: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{aligned} -& Δ_N u = |x|^{Nα} e^u \quad \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N && , \\ & \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |x|^{Nα} e^u \, dx -1$ when $N=2$. Since it is not based on complex analysis, this alternative and more PDE-oriented approach naturally extends to $N\geq 3$ by providing the classification for any $-1 0$, a hint that non-radial solutions might arise for $α>0$ as it happens when $N=2$.
